raw_case_text: A twenty-nine-year-old male presented with a history of fever with chills and rigor for 19 days, evening rise in temperature, which responded to paracetamol. Pulse rate was 90 per minute, blood pressure was 112/78 mm of Hg, and SpO2 was 98% on room air. General examination revealed no hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory investigations showed hemoglobin of 12.3 gm/dL, and leucocyte counts of 8900/muL with a platelet count of 1.8 lakhs/muL and ESR was 98 mm/hr. Chest X-ray was normal. Urine routine examination was normal. Malarial smears were negative. Ciprofloxacin was given empirically outside for 5 days. Ceftriaxone was started empirically; blood cultures were sent which showed S. typhi growth on the third day with sensitivity to ceftriaxone. The patient didn't respond to sensitive antibiotics till day 7. Meanwhile, the Mantoux test was done which showed a 14 mm induration. We did a CT scan which showed terminal ileal concentric thickening of size 8 mm of length 9 cm. The patient underwent a colonoscopy which showed a normal colon till caecum, but the ileocecal valve showed multiple small superficial ulcers with whitish exudate on both lips. Ileum till 15 cm showed edematous, reddish bluish mucosa, less distensible, circumferential superficial ulcer near to ileocecal valve extending to the length of 3 cm with a few other small superficial ulcers till 30 cm (Fig. 1). Biopsies from the ulcer showed acute inflammation mixed with sheets of histiocyte infiltration (Fig. 2). No distortion of crypt architecture or well-defined epithelioid granuloma was noted. Ziehl Neelsen (ZN) stains did not reveal acid-fast bacilli, and Gene Xpert was negative. Intravenous antibiotics continued, and the patient improved on day 11. Antibiotics were continued for 5 more days. The patient was discharged, repeat colonoscopy was done 6 weeks later which showed normal ileum.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 29-year-old male presented with a 19-day history of fever with chills and rigors.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with fever, chills, and rigors for 19 days, marked by evening temperature elevations that responded temporarily to paracetamol. Prior to hospital admission, he was empirically treated with oral ciprofloxacin for 5 days without clinical improvement.
subjective.past_medical_history: Received empirical oral ciprofloxacin for 5 days outside prior to admission. No other chronic illnesses reported.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports chills, rigors, and evening spikes in temperature. Denies other systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: Pulse rate 90 beats/min, blood pressure 112/78 mmHg, SpO2 98% on room air. General physical examination revealed no hepatosplenomegaly.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 12.3 gm/dL, leucocyte count 8900/muL, platelet count 1.8 lakhs/muL, and ESR 98 mm/hr. Chest X-ray was normal. Routine urinalysis was normal. Malarial smears were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Mantoux tuberculin skin test showed 14 mm induration. Abdominal CT revealed concentric thickening of the terminal ileum measuring 8 mm in wall thickness over a length of 9 cm. Colonoscopy showed normal mucosa up to the caecum; ileocecal valve exhibited multiple small superficial ulcers with whitish exudate on both lips; ileum up to 15 cm showed edematous, reddish-bluish, less distensible mucosa with a circumferential superficial ulcer (length 3 cm) near the ileocecal valve, and several small superficial ulcers extending up to 30 cm. Histopathological examination of ulcer biopsies showed acute inflammation mixed with sheets of histiocytic infiltration without crypt architecture distortion or well-defined epithelioid granulomas. Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) stain was negative for acid-fast bacilli and GeneXpert was negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Salmonella typhi bacteremia (typhoid fever) confirmed by blood cultures demonstrating S. typhi growth on the third day of incubation, susceptible to ceftriaxone. Intestinal tuberculosis (Koch's disease) was ruled out based on negative ZN stain, negative GeneXpert, and absence of granulomas on biopsy; malaria was ruled out by negative smears.
Plan & Outcome: Treated with intravenous ceftriaxone. The patient did not respond to sensitive antibiotics through day 7, with clinical defervescence and improvement occurring on day 11. Ceftriaxone was continued for an additional 5 days (total 16 days). The patient was discharged, and a repeat colonoscopy at 6 weeks demonstrated a completely normal ileum.
